results.claim: The revised receiver extended 370 mm and a released pipe stayed in the trough
results.conditions: Continuous underside lands cleared the two absorber caps. With a 54 mm greater dock setback, 48 modeled launches reached sustained support across both sectors.
results.limit: The dock was supplied independently. The study assumes a belt exit speed and grants zero match deliveries.

results.claim: The loaded robot braked with its first pipe still aboard
results.conditions: On the two signed wheel paths the fixed camera lost its height bound. Encoders and gyro confirmed a stop at 31.960 or 30.120 s. The pipe moved at most 0.507 or 0.351 mm during each attempt.
results.limit: The receiver has yet to carry the observed pipe from either stop to the scoring dock.

results.claim: The stowed fallback earned five points in both modeled matches
results.conditions: Two empty-start runs at 65 and 72 kg cleared the starting line at the end of AUTO and held their numbered bumper in the red barge zone through assessment. Both runs lasted 156 seconds including disabled time.
results.limit: The south lane was reserved. Keeping the partner in its usual slot overlaps the starting footprint. The two-pipe scoring route is a separate study.

results.claim: The swerve robot reached the station before the first feed
results.conditions: The corrected drive model reached its docking gate at 20.285 s and 20.330 s for the two 65 kg approaches. Both 72 kg cases also docked before the scheduled 21.100 s feed.
results.limit: The opening film illustrates the earlier drive model. The corrected first feed and first loaded motion have a separate camera and contact replay.

results.claim: The receiver retained its first pipe through 71.8 mm of swerve travel
results.conditions: All four signed arrival and contact-refinement runs retained the same pipe through finite braking. Both stereo heads agreed in all 88 moving exposures per run under the wheel-angle mask.
results.limit: Missing a fixed-eye image stopped the drive. Full loaded travel to the scoring dock and a witnessed release remain open.

results.claim: Five timely stereo observations confirmed the seated pipe
results.conditions: On the first-feed R4 study, the fixed head located the pipe and the roof head saw its rear edge. Both signed approaches agreed at both simulation time steps.
results.limit: Matching pipe and shelf finishes hid the rear edge in every required capture. At 45 ms transport delay only three good observations arrived in time. The controller held in both cases.

results.claim: The R4 inspection budget leaves 170 g of mass margin
results.conditions: The numbered R4 assembly matches the mass register. Four populated modules at their receiving allowance and the specified cable cuts put the upper estimate at 51.993 kg against the 52.163 kg limit.
results.limit: Uniform one-metre supply cuts put this case 4.9 g over. The mass calculation uses component estimates and planned wire lengths.

build.configuration: Follow the release-day field lab, adopted match role, mechanism CAD, sensor tests and complete match-clock evidence through the project's documents.

Four swerve modules sit on a 564 mm wheelbase and 554 mm track. The public model points all four wheels forward to show the layout. The independently reopened R4 Fusion robot retains all 1,096 supplier module bodies and their original fork positions. Fusion also verified all 948 project solids, including the 16 white bumper digits.
The shelf and guide arms sit above the four independently steered wheels. The public view shows the receiver stowed and both red bumper covers installed.
Two red covers wrap the chassis. White 1780 numerals read from each outward face. The side markings stay on individual covers so the two halves can separate for service.

media.description: Three-dimensional cutaways show a station feed seating the hollow pipe, the sliding receiver extending, and the released pipe settling in a red trough.
media.caption: The station pickup plays at 2x. At the separate scoring dock, the 370 mm extension and the trough landing play in real time. A cut at the rim identifies the assumed belt exit speed.
The robot clears its starting line in AUTO, waits while disabled, then returns to park. The clock shows the full 156 seconds. Playback speeds up during the long hold.
media.description: A top-down view of the numbered R4 CAD moving over the starting line and back into the red zone, with the current mode, position and playback speed.

media.caption: Nominal approach at real time. The field view shows the path to the station. The four-wheel diagram follows simulated steering and rolling speeds at 10 frames per second.
media.description: A field replay beside four labeled wheel directions, with the match clock and station event visible.

media.caption: The fixed camera still locates the pipe when its finish matches the shelf. The roof camera loses the rear edge. Both views must agree before the controller can confirm grip.
media.description: Five of five observations qualify with visible edges and a 15 ms delay. Matching finishes qualify zero. Increasing the delay to 45 ms qualifies three of five.
